papers.title: Integrating niches of the pathogen, multiple host and vector species highlights abiotic constraints and host‐vector interactions shaping pine wilt disease risk in China
papers.authors: Wang Wen-quan, Ting Du, Jiangxia Ye, Xiaohong Huang, Yangyang Li
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pine wilt disease (PWD), caused by Bursaphelenchus xylophilus (PWN), is a major threat to forest health and pest management in China. Because PWD results from interactions among the pathogen, vector insects, and host plants, single-component analyses may misrepresent disease risk and overlook species-specific contributions. We integrated the environmental niches of the pathogen, hosts, and vectors to characterize abiotic constraints and biotic influences on PWD risk, quantify species-specific contributions and interactions, and inform surveillance priorities. RESULTS: Ensemble ecological niche models were developed for PWN, 17 susceptible hosts, and 10 potential cerambycid vectors across China and integrated with GeoDetector analysis. Although suitability patterns were broadly consistent, PWN had a much narrower suitable range than hosts and vectors, and this concordance declined under future climate scenarios. Bioclimatic variables were the primary determinants of habitat suitability for most species, whereas PWN showed narrower optimal ranges for key environmental drivers than most hosts and vectors. papers.title: A model for the spatial population dynamics of the European invasion of the Japanese beetle (Popillia japonica)
papers.authors: Davide Martinetti, Laura Erbetta, Danièle Bevacqua, Olivier Bonnefon, Marino Gatto
papers.abstract: Popillia japonica is an invasive beetle first detected in Northern Italy in 2014 and considered as one of the most dangerous pests for crops due to the economic, environmental, and social costs by European phytosanitary authorities. Here we develop a process-based model for quantifying the invasion dynamics of P. japonica with the goal to elaborate risk maps for the design of surveillance and control strategies. The proposed spatially heterogeneous model captures the different behaviors of both adults, which drive the invasion through flight and short-distance human-mediated transport, and ovo-larval stages, which affect demography due to their susceptibility to environmental conditions. Both processes are biologically informed through variables that are known to influence population dynamics, namely the number of summer days, affecting the flight ability of the adults, and the environmental suitability for larval survival. The simulated presence of adult beetles is then contrasted to pest observation data at the municipality scale from Northern Italy and Switzerland from the initial invasion to December 2023. papers.title: Overcoming insect pest challenges for sustainable rice production in the Americas
papers.authors: Roland Bocco, Stanley Omar PB. Samonte, Kimberly S. Ponce, Esther Pegalepo, Zakaria Hossain Prodhan
papers.abstract: Rice production in the Americas has expanded to meet a rising demand, but insect pests continue to threaten yields, grain quality, and farmer incomes. This review synthesizes current knowledge of the major insect pests affecting rice systems across the Americas and evaluates the performance, trade-offs, and complementarities of existing and emerging controls. It describes regional pest complexes, such as rice water weevil in the United States, Hoja Blanca vectors and stem borers in tropical areas, and late-season stink bugs across the continent. It examines how climate change, land use, and trade change invasion risk and pest activity timing. The review examines integrated pest management components: surveillance that blends field/edge scouting with decision-support tools and predictive modeling; cultural and agronomic practices that reduce baseline risk; biological control via parasitoids, predators, and entomopathogens using classical, augmentative, and conservation strategies; and threshold-based chemical control emphasizing resistance management, and residue stewardship. Innovative approaches, including AI-enabled forecasting, genomics-assisted resistance, and RNA interference

papers.title: Geospatial assessment of Japanese encephalitis virus infection risk in Australia
papers.authors: Lucinda E. Harrison, David H. Duncan, Jennifer A. Flegg, David J. Price, Nina Kurucz
papers.abstract: Japanese encephalitis virus (JEV) is a leading cause of viral encephalitis in humans in Asia. Prior to 2021, only sporadic outbreaks had been detected in Australia's tropical northern extremes. However, during 2021-23, JEV infection was identified in 45 people and in more than 85 piggeries, together with many detections in feral pigs, mosquitoes, and other livestock across Australia, including in the temperate far south. Here we estimated the spatial extent of virus transmission during the outbreak (the realised niche) and the area environmentally suitable for transmission (the potential niche). We collated a national dataset of JEV surveillance and detection in humans, mosquitoes, domestic pigs, feral pigs, and sentinel chickens from 2021-23. We combined these data with (1) previously published predictions of habitat suitability for vertebrate host and vector species, and (2) estimated densities of humans, domestic pigs, and feral pigs, in a multipart assessment of spatial risk. papers.title: Citizen Science and Environmental DNA Reveals Site of an Invasive Paropsisterna beata (Newman) (Coleoptera: Chrysomelidae) Population in New Zealand
papers.authors: Toni M. Withers, Andrew R. Pugh, Darryl A. Herron, Dean Satchell, Shaun Wilkinson
papers.source: OpenAlex / New Zealand Journal of Zoology
papers.abstract: More than a decade after being declared eradicated, a population of the Australian blessed leaf beetle Paropsisterna beata (Coleoptera: Chrysomelidae) was located in New Zealand in 2026. The pest has been found and photographed three times by citizen scientists approximately 25 km north of the original Wellington infestation and reported on iNaturalist. An environmental DNA (eDNA) match from a water sample then directed searching to Eucalyptus trees visible on Google Earth upstream. This sequence of events leading to finding an established population highlights the potential for citizen science observations and eDNA monitoring to both uncover and pinpoint a cryptic pest's location as part of biosecurity surveillance.

papers.authors: Wei Yang, Hongwei Zhou, Haochang Hu, Wenlu Wang, Haojie Zhang
papers.abstract: Pine wilt disease (PWD) is one of the most destructive invasive forest diseases in China, yet the environmental drivers underlying its spatially heterogeneous spread remain poorly understood. This study aimed to characterize the spatial and temporal patterns of natural PWD dispersal, identify persistent hotspots, and determine region-specific environmental drivers of PWD habitat suitability. We developed an integrated framework combining dispersal screening, biomod2 ensemble modelling, SaTScan spatiotemporal scan statistics, and Geographical Pattern Causality (GPC) analysis to examine PWD spread and its environmental drivers at national and regional scales. Natural dispersal increased markedly after 2016 and reached a peak of 9728 newly affected subcompartments in 2020. At the national scale, Altitude, mean diurnal temperature range (Bio2), and normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) were the dominant determinants of habitat suitability, with relative importance values of 27.52%, 25.29%, and 21.87%, respectively. papers.title: Mechanisms of Pesticide Stress Responses and Green Mitigation Approaches in Astragalus membranaceus
papers.authors: Shanshan Zhao
papers.abstract: Pesticide application is essential for managing pests in medicinal plants, yet it inevitably introduces risks of pesticide residue accumulation, plant growth inhibition, and changes in the biosynthesis of bioactive compounds. Understanding the responses of medicinal plants to pesticide stress and developing effective approaches for reducing pesticide toxicity are important for the safe production of medicinal materials. Using Astragalus membranaceus as a model medicinal plant, this dissertation systematically investigates the uptake, translocation, metabolism, and phytotoxicity of three representative pesticides, including tebuconazole (TEB), atrazine (ATZ), and avermectin (AVM). In addition, two approaches for alleviating pesticide stress and reducing residues, namely endogenous hormone regulation and rhizosphere microbial remediation, were further evaluated. All pesticides exhibited distinct patterns of uptake and distribution in A. membranaceus. ATZ was readily transported to the shoots, whereas TEB mainly accumulated in the roots and AVM showed very limited transport within the plant. papers.title: Sensitivity evaluation and multi-omics analysis of Bursaphelenchus xylophilus populations to emamectin benzoate in Shandong province field
papers.authors: Kunyang Ju, Zhifan Ma, Shuhan Guo, YuKe Wang, Shengnan Dong
papers.abstract: Pine trees provide substantial ecological and economic benefits worldwide, including water conservation, timber production, and carbon sequestration. However, Bursaphelenchus xylophilus , as the pathogen of pine wilt disease (PWD), results in extensive pine mortality annually, posing a serious threat to global pine resources and environmental security. Currently, chemical control remains the primary strategy for managing PWD. In Shandong Province, emamectin benzoate (EB) is the main nematicide for trunk injection. Nevertheless, long-term use of a single compound carries a high risk of resistance development. In this study, the sensitivity of 15 B. xylophilus strains from different regions of Shandong Province to EB was evaluated. The highest and lowest LC 50 values were observed in the PL (320.99 μg•mL -1 ) and CD strains (114.63 μg•mL -1 ), respectively, yielding a resistance ratio (PL vs CD) of 2.8 < 5, indicating that EB resistance may not have developed in the B. xylophilus populations in Shandong. papers.title: Living with Wilt: Disease, Control, and Plantation Ecologies in Chinese Banana Farming in Cambodia
papers.authors: Mingze Gao
papers.abstract: Drawing on fieldwork conducted in August 2026 at four Chinese-invested banana enterprises in Cambodia and interviews with a biotechnology supplier, this article examines how plant disease is understood, managed, and experienced within plantation production. Managers, technical specialists, and Cambodian workers offered overlapping explanations centred on fungi, bacteria, mixed infections, continuous cultivation, and insects. These accounts reflected differences in occupational responsibilities, training, and exposure to economic risk. Yet causal explanations did not translate straightforwardly into control practices: actors with similar diagnoses adopted different interventions, while those with different explanations converged on the same cultivar or microbial products. Access to capital, professional experience, commercial interests, and perceived limitations in public plant-health support mediated these choices. Cultivar replacement emerged as the principal response, alongside soil amendments, biological products, and chemical treatments. papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

papers.title: Cascading effects of soil water content on leaf chemistry and damage: implications for plant susceptibility to pests and pathogens in a drier world
papers.authors: Álvaro Gaytán, Luis Matías, Óscar Godoy, Ignacio Manuel Pérez-Ramos, Pablo Homet
papers.abstract: Climate change is causing major alterations in precipitation regimes and soil water availability, with far-reaching effects on plant traits. Changes in plant chemistry under drought scenarios are particularly relevant, as they can modulate plant interactions with antagonistic organisms. However, how such changes in plant chemistry affect plant susceptibility to biotic damage remains poorly understood. Here we integrated results from a systematic literature review and a field study in Mediterranean mixed forests to advance our understanding of the cascading effects of reduced soil water content on leaf reserves, defences and damage caused by herbivores and pathogens. The literature review revealed that studies linking soil water content with leaf chemistry and damage remain scarce and reported a variety of direct and indirect relationships between the three components. Nevertheless, most studies found higher leaf damage under drier conditions. Results from our field study also supported that leaf damage increased with decreasing soil water content, a relationship largely mediated by changes in leaf phenolic compounds. Methods. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 262 patients who underwent surgical revascularization between January 2019 and June 2023. Results. papers.abstract: Hypoxia is closely associated with tumor progression, metastasis, therapeutic resistance, and diagnostic challenges. The timely detection of hypoxia in live cancer cells is critical for early cancer diagnosis and for monitoring the effectiveness of anticancer therapies. Recently, there has been growing interest in non-covalent supramolecular design strategies for the development of hypoxia-sensitive sensors and prodrugs. Unlike the widely employed covalent approach, supramolecular chemistry eliminates the need for complex and time-consuming synthetic processes. Instead, the individual components of the sensor autonomously self-assemble into the desired structure. This review provides an overview of hypoxia-targeted and hypoxia-activated supramolecular probes, along with their mechanisms of action in tumor diagnosis and therapy. The supramolecular systems considered are classified according to the use of certain classes of macrocycles. The role of macrocyclic derivatives in the various proposed approaches and the response patterns of hypoxic targets will also be analyzed. papers.authors: KRISHNA SANDEEP JONNALA, K VENKAT RAJU
papers.source: OpenAlex / International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
papers.abstract: Image classification remains a foundational problem in computer vision, underpinning applications that range from medical diagnostics to autonomous navigation. Although deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have substantially advanced classification accuracy over the last decade, standard architectures such as VGG, ResNet, and plain CNNs often struggle to jointly optimize accuracy, parameter efficiency, and robustness to intra-class variation. This paper proposes an AttentionGuided Refinement Network (AGR-Net), a CNN architecture that integrates a lightweight channel-and-spatial attention module with residual feature refinement blocks to improve discriminative feature learning while maintaining a compact parameter footprint. The proposed model is evaluated on the CIFAR-10 benchmark dataset using a rigorous experimental protocol that includes data augmentation, learning-rate scheduling, and five-fold cross-validation. papers.title: Application of medical gases in prevention and treatment of electromagnetic radiation injury.
papers.authors: Yun Xing, Fengxu Chen, Gonggeng Liu, Shijun Bao, Xujian Zhang
papers.abstract: The widespread proliferation of electromagnetic technologies in communications, healthcare, and daily life poses increasing risks of radiation-induced tissue injury. Mitigating these deleterious effects remains a formidable challenge. Recently, medical gases, including molecular hydrogen (H2), hydrogen sulfide (H2S), carbon monoxide (CO), nitric oxide (NO), and hyperbaric oxygen, have emerged as a promising therapeutic modality with radioprotective potential. These gases exert their effects through integrated, anti-inflammatory, anti-apoptotic, and mitochondrial-protective mechanisms. Specifically, the endogenous gasotransmitters (CO, NO, and H2S) modulate precise signaling networks, while the exogenous interventions (H2, and hyperbaric oxygen) function primarily through direct radical scavenging or the induction of hormetic stress responses. This review evaluates the research progress of these five medical gases in preventing and treating injuries across the electromagnetic spectrum. H2 possesses the broadest evidence base, particularly in radiofrequency and ultraviolet protection. H2S and CO demonstrate potent efficacy in addressing ultraviolet-induced skin and retinal damage. papers.title: Exploring the effective management of potato upstream food loss and waste policy in Scotland - circular economy approach
papers.authors: Stephanie Isioma Nwachokor
papers.source: OpenAlex / Edinburgh Napier Research Repository (Edinburgh Napier University)
papers.abstract: Food Loss and Waste [FLW] is a contributor to food insecurity and environmentally unsustainable practices. Extensive studies have explored food loss and waste in the downstream sector (e.g. homes, restaurants, and others), with less attention paid to upstream loss and waste. Emerging evidence suggests that upstream potato waste is increasingly contributing to environmental degradation, thereby undermining the attainment of the circular economy (CE) and contributing to the growth of greenhouse gases (GHG). Employing a unique cross-sectional, qualitative research design grounded in interpretivist principles, this study delves into the perspectives of stakeholders within the Scottish upstream potato food chain. papers.abstract: Background Aedes mosquito-borne diseases, such as dengue fever, pose significant challenges to global public health. Mosquito management is regarded as one of the most critical measures to control these diseases. Temephos has been widely used for larval mosquito control, but its sustained application has resulted in the emergence of resistance in many regions in China. Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis (Bti) offers an environmentally friendly alternative, but its field efficacy against late-instar larvae is limited. Previous studies have demonstrated the synergistic potential of combining temephos and Bti. Therefore, this study aims to determine the most effective combination ratio through laboratory bioassays and to evaluate the practical efficacy of this mixed formulation under field conditions. papers.authors: Phoebe A. O., Tunwari B. A., Yakubu U.
papers.source: OpenAlex / Kwaghe International Journal of Sciences and Technology
papers.abstract: Bacterial fruit blotch (BFB), caused by Acidovorax citrulli, severely limits watermelon (Citrullus lanatus) production. Concerns about environmental pollution, pathogen resistance, and food safety associated with synthetic bactericides highlight the need for sustainable management alternatives. This study evaluated the combined effects of botanical extracts and varietal selection on BFB suppression and watermelon yield in the Guinea Savannah agroecological zone of Taraba State, Nigeria. Field experiments were conducted at Wukari and Ardo Kola during the 2020 and 2021 cropping seasons using a 4 × 5 factorial arrangement in a randomized complete block design with three replications. Four varieties—Sugar Baby, Charleston Gray, Crimson Sweet, and Kaolack—were evaluated under five treatments: neem (Azadirachta indica) extract, jatropha (Jatropha curcas) extract, combined neem and jatropha extracts, copper hydroxide, and an untreated control. papers.title: RNA Interference for Precision Management of Plant-Parasitic Nematodes: Mechanisms, Delivery Constraints and Translational Evidence
papers.authors: Vadaga Dhanasri, Swadhin Kumar Swain, Rudraboyina Sai Kiran, Huzaifah Ashaq, Sukriti Saha
papers.source: OpenAlex / PLANT CELL BIOTECHNOLOGY AND MOLECULAR BIOLOGY
papers.abstract: Plant-parasitic nematodes are persistent constraints on crop productivity because their behaviour, protected habitats and intimate relationships with host roots complicate both diagnosis and control. RNA interference offers sequence-guided suppression of nematode gene expression without requiring a conventional toxicant to act on a broad physiological target. Yet molecular specificity should not be conflated with biological control, and promising experiments have produced uneven results across species, life stages, delivery systems and scales. This critical narrative review examines research on double-stranded RNA exposure, target validation, host-induced gene silencing, artificial microRNAs, non-transgenic formulations, nanocarriers and translation to field use. Peer-reviewed experimental and methodological studies published through 14 August 2026 were considered, with seminal earlier work included to establish the mechanism. The strongest evidence concerns gene knockdown and reduced infection or reproduction in controlled plant systems, particularly root-knot and cyst nematodes. papers.title: Before Qualia, Strategic Existence Begins
papers.authors: Angelina Inesia-Forde
papers.abstract: Before evolution can select anything, a physically possible causal architecture must already exist for selection to exploit. The T4 bacteriophage, a mindless nanoscale machine whose structure executes functions that map onto both empowering and disempowering strategies in Forde's framework of social dynamics, demonstrates this principle at the nanoscale. The strategies mapped include security, knowledge, hope, fairness, unity, and dignity, alongside their darker counterparts: nativism, hierarchy, misinformation, subjugation, dehumanization, and fear. Each concept is paired with a specific biological mechanism, virion stability, irreversible adsorption, superinfection exclusion, among others, showing that the mapping is grounded in observable structure. These mappings do not reify nonhuman organisms or attribute human qualities to mindless machines. They are structural descriptions: the concepts name functions that the architecture performs, not feelings that the organism experiences. papers.authors: Chun Hua Liu
papers.source: OpenAlex / Edinburgh Napier Research Repository (Edinburgh Napier University)
papers.abstract: The building sector is the third largest contributor to anthropogenic greenhouse gas emission in Canada. The carbon mitigation from the sector is critically important to achieve the goal of net-zero emission by 2050. Residential buildings are a key driver of energy consumption and emissions from the sector. While the operation of building becomes more efficient, the selection of low embodied carbon and energy materials is increasingly becoming key aspect of any decarbonisation strategy aimed at the built environment. Insulation materials are among the most important building parts to achieve energy conservation in buildings. Mainstream insulation materials, typically made from fossil-based raw sources, usually score a remarkably high embodied carbon and energy footprint. Hemp is widely recognized as among one of the most used biobased insulation raw materials in buildings due to its thermal properties and better overall environmental performances than that of mainstream insulations. papers.authors: Deepali Rustagi, Kunal, Rohit Kumar, Pankaj Kumar, Atin Kumar
papers.source: OpenAlex / Frontiers in Bioengineering and Biotechnology
papers.abstract: Global health continues to be impacted by viral diseases, and this poses a need for timely diagnosis, potent antiviral treatment, and flexible prevention. To tackle these problems, nanotechnology has become an incredibly flexible tool for viral detection, therapeutic delivery, vaccination and biomimetic material design. Recent developments in the field of nano-enabled virology will be reviewed and will focus on the use of nanomaterials in the development of biosensors and diagnostic platforms to make virus detection more sensitive, specific, faster and more portable. It also explores the antiviral activity of metallic, polymeric, lipid-based, carbon-based and 2D nanomaterials, including MXenes, their ability to directly inactivate viruses and targeted delivery of antiviral agents and nucleic acids, etc. Special focus is placed on lipid nanoparticles as carriers for RNA therapeutics and mRNA vaccines, and novel vaccine strategies based on peptides, proteins, virus-like particles, and DNA. papers.abstract: The increasing prevalence of hostel squatting in Nigerian public universities has raised concerns about its implications for students' psychosocial well-being and academic outcomes. This study investigated hostel squatting as a predictor of academic achievement, interpersonal relationship and emotional adjustment among squatting undergraduate students in Federal University of Technology Owerri in Imo State. A predictive correlational survey design was adopted. papers.abstract: An estimated 200 million cases of viral pneumonia occur annually, with the most prominent causes being Rhinovirus and Influenza, with limited treatment options available. LL-37 is a human host defence peptide produced as part of the innate immune system that has direct antiviral and immunomodulatory properties. However, the use of LL-37 as a therapeutic agent is limited due to inhibitory and degradative potential in biological environments. A form of nanocellulose known as cellulose nanofibrils have shown multiple characteristics that make it an attractive drug delivery candidate for LL-37. These include a high surface area-to-volume ratio, abundance of hydroxyl groups that can be modified for drug loading and swelling capabilities allowing for sustained release of encapsulated drugs. However, current nanocellulose manufacturing processes are commercially infeasible due to high energy expenditure and may lead to indirect cytotoxicity due to pre-treatment methods. papers.authors: Federica Mascherpa
papers.source: OpenAlex / Edinburgh Napier Research Repository (Edinburgh Napier University)
papers.abstract: While academic scholars such as Robert Foulke – in his recognition of Conrad’s James Wait as a Jonah in The Sea Voyage Narrative (2002) – have noted the presence of sailors’ superstitious beliefs within nineteenth-century seafaring narratives, they treat these beliefs as peripheral to the narratives and often dismiss them as connotators of sailors’ ignorance. This thesis will reverse this understanding and, instead, demonstrate that such superstition is a fundamental – and not marginal – element within nineteenth-century seafaring literature which engages meaningfully with narrative themes and has a profound influence on linguistic register, preconceived notions of genre, narrative structures and, overall, our general understanding of the sea environment. To achieve this, my thesis draws upon a range of historical materials, from logbooks to compendiums of superstitions to contemporaneous chapbooks and ballads, the close reading of nineteenth century nautical narratives, and an understanding of narrative structures founded upon a narratological basis. papers.title: Recent plant photosynthate as a driver of ecological and evolutionary processes
papers.authors: David Johnson, Hannah M. Griffiths
papers.abstract: Summary Plants rapidly allocate carbon from photosynthesis belowground via root exudates and root‐associated microorganisms. Here we synthesise recent evidence of our understanding of the consequences of this ‘fast’ pathway of recent photosynthate flux for major ecological and evolutionary processes. This rapid input of plant‐derived carbon to soils shapes food webs and drives processes including soil CO 2 efflux, nutrient cycling, plant community dynamics, stability of symbioses and evolution of contrasting modes of nutrition, such as parasitism and mycoheterotrophy. We also highlight how seasonality and anthropogenic and natural perturbations likely determine the magnitude and dynamics of this fast pathway across major vegetation types, but these factors remain understudied. Further gaps in understanding include demonstrating causal links between photosynthate flow and key biogeochemical cycling processes and the capture of photosynthate by co‐occurring root‐associated microorganisms.
